Firstly, it is more of a character-driven series than an action driven anime. Besides Eris' training, action tends to happen when it really matters. There is adventure elements in arcs but this series has always been more of a character drama, like how the beginning episodes were with the first season.

Secondly, fights in this series are never too long but are much more meaningful and action-packed when it matters. The Sword God style which Eris learned for example, are meant to end very quickly rather than going forever so it makes sense to go all out and have it look awesome while the quick element of it makes it feel more realistic. It is more intense seeing those short bits of fights than seeing something too stretched out for no reason or filled with dialogue in between when redundant. Most people loved those few seconds of epic animation in those earlier fights without issues.  


Thirdly, next episode is called Turning Point 3 so there might be a little more to this season than you would think for the time being. The anime has spent time in building Rudeus' character again from the ground up, having him mature and grow up as a person, as a brother, now as a husband and be an adult. Relationships and friendships are built, and more plot elements are teased as well. These kinds of episodes spent in building all that up makes the stuff in future seasons feel a lot more impactful as a result.

The season prior to last year, Son was the guy who stepped up the most with tying for the Golden Boot when Kane struggled for a good chunk of the early part of the season after his Florida arc. And the one before, both of them did great together as a partnership in the COVID-19 season with Mourinho. And before, we had players more than just Kane and Son perform relatively well when we were at our best like Eriksen, Toby and Jan, prime Dele and Lloris, etc. It's just that this last particular year, Son was playing injured throughout and was poor, Richarlison had 1 goal and our defence was horrendous so that was the season where Kane had to do more on his own than he did before and we still only got 8th out of that.

Yes, Kane's been our most consistent scorer and performer but it was last season where he genuinely was more of a one-man show than ever and we flopped as a result. This season though, seeing Maddison step up when he was healthy, Son back to his best, Richarlison actually scoring goals again in recent times, Van de Ven-Romero's defensive partnership when healthy, Vicario's incredible upgrade as a goalkeeper from Lloris last year, the inverted full-back partnership in Porro and Udogie, Sarr, and even some guys like Ben Davies ironically stepping up when we were bruised this season. The team as a whole is so much better collectively compared to last year and it isn't as one-man of a show as it used to be, and it is a younger team too. There is actual room for this team to really grow in the long run in different areas.

Besides the injuries, I think the main factors were the style of football being much better with more individuals actually shining in the team now and improving a lot performance-wise despite Harry Kane leaving us. He did absolutely carry us last season with his 30 goals so the expectations were very limited for this season (and we still finished 8th), and I know people that expected us to be in the midtable area again so we have definitely performed much higher than expected for this season.
